The bill would allow money to be taken from the Consolidated Revenue Fund to cover any debts the Commonwealth owes under a Pacific banking guarantee.
It would appropriate funds from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for that purpose.
The bill would start on 1 July 2025.
The bill appropriates money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund.
The bill covers liabilities under a Pacific banking guarantee.
The Commonwealth and any parties involved in a Pacific banking guarantee are affected.

Moved the Pacific Banking Guarantee Bill 2025, which would allow the Commonwealth to guarantee eligible Australian banks' Pacific operations against a possible regional default, while noting broader efforts to maintain banking access, support regional communities, and strengthen financial systems.

Supported the Pacific Banking Guarantee Bill 2025 while seeking Senate committee scrutiny of taxpayer risks, transparency and possible amendments. The debate contrasted competing records of aid, security, diplomacy and development assistance in the Pacific, and argued that maintaining banking services was important to Australia's strategic engagement and regional prosperity.
